children: will be reporting earnings this Tuesday morning. Here’s what to look for.

Dollar Tree beat analysts’ revenue expectations last quarter, reporting revenues of $4.89 billion, up 7% year on year. It was a mixed quarter for the company, with a beat of analysts’ EPS estimates but EPS guidance for next quarter missing analysts’ expectations significantly.
Is Dollar Tree a buy or sell going into earnings?

params.linkText: Read our full analysis here, it’s free for active Edge members

children: This quarter, the market is expecting Dollar Tree’s revenue to grow 6.1% year on year, slowing from the 9.4% increase it recorded in the same quarter last year.

Analysts covering the company have generally reconfirmed their estimates over the last 30 days, suggesting they anticipate the business will stay the course heading into earnings. Dollar Tree has missed Wall Street’s revenue estimates multiple times over the last two years.

Looking at Dollar Tree’s peers in the non-discretionary retail segment, some have already reported their Q3 results, giving us a hint as to what we can expect. BJ's delivered year-on-year revenue growth of 17.5%, beating analysts’ expectations by 5.2%, and Target reported revenues up 7.1%, topping estimates by 2%. Target traded up 5% following the results.

Investors in the non-discretionary retail segment have had steady hands going into earnings, with share prices flat over the last month. Dollar Tree is up 11.1% during the same time and is heading into earnings with an average analyst price target of $137.67 (compared to the current share price of $138.80).
